key_insight: A biologically inspired spiking network trained with e-prop achieved 100% survival in evaluation, matching backpropagation through time while more biologically faithful alternatives performed substantially worse.
engineering_relevance: The study informs humanoid locomotion controller design by quantifying trade-offs between biological plausibility and control performance.
method: Distill a reinforcement learning expert policy using dataset aggregation.
Compare frozen recurrent weights, reward-modulated STDP, e-prop, and backpropagation through time.
Evaluate locomotion performance and demonstrate brief stepping on a full-size Unitree H1-2.
evidence_signal: Reported survival rates were 100% for e-prop and backpropagation through time, approximately 43.7% for the fixed reservoir, and approximately 11% for reward-modulated STDP.
watch_item: Brief hardware stepping does not establish sustained real-world locomotion robustness, and the abstract does not specify survival-test conditions.
paper_title: Controlling the Humanoid Robot H1-2 With a Simulated Biologically Plausible Network
